messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: elevated 5xx and auth failures originating in us-east-1. Affected surfaces: Hosted API ingress, several Dedicated pools in us-east-1. Root signals: increased error rate from AWS STS and CloudWatch ingest failures. Severity: S2.
alice (oncall): grabbing this. seeing spikes ~15:12 UTC. +1000 5xx/min on edge-api-us-east. auth errors correlate with STS 500 responses.
bob (sre): confirming. logs show 50% of token fetches hitting 500s, bucketed at 15:11-15:14. also CloudWatch put-metric 5xxs so our observability is partial. running quick check: ```curl -sS "https://sts.amazonaws.com/?Action=GetCallerIdentity&Version=2011-06-15" | head -n 1``` returns an error timeout for some AZs.
carla (eng-runtime): looks like third-party (AWS control plane) degradation causing cascading token refresh failures. mitigation options: 1) route new Hosted API traffic to eu-west-1 pools, 2) enable token-caching fallback for Dedicated pools to avoid refreshing for short TTLs, 3) reduce client retry storms.
dave (support): we already have two customers in prod reporting elevated 502s. opening tickets and flagging priority. prepping a short customer note.
alice (oncall): bob, can you flip the routing policy for hosted-us-east -> prefer eu-west for new sessions? we should fail open to cached tokens where safe. I can update routing policy now.
bob (sre): doing routing change (manual override) now. command: ```redwoodctl routing set --region preference hosted-api us-east1:low eu-west1:high --until 2026-03-17T17:00Z``` will apply. applying... :gear:
bob (sre): applied. monitoring ingress: error rate dropped ~40% for new connections routed to eu-west. existing cached sessions still hitting us-east backends.
carla (eng-runtime): deploying token-cache-fallback patch to Dedicated pools (reduce token refresh cadence from 5m -> 30m) to avoid hitting STS. rolling to us-east dedicated node group 1/3.. 2/3..
emma (product): preparing status page draft: short note about third-party AWS control plane issue affecting auth & metrics in us-east-1, mitigation in progress. earliest ETA TBD.
dave (support): sending proactive messages to impacted accounts: doc snippet ready: "We're experiencing elevated errors in us-east-1 caused by an AWS control-plane incident. We're routing traffic to other regions and applying safe token caching. Monitoring closely."
alice (oncall): handing off to carla for night watch. I'm going offline in 20m. carla, take pager. key TODOs: watch error rates, rollback routing once STS stabilizes, coordinate with AWS support ticket.
carla (eng-runtime): ack taking pager. subscribing to AWS trust events and support case. I'll escalate if error rate >10% for >10m.
incident-bot: AWS support case opened ID: 1234567890. Notified account team.
carla (eng-runtime): observed CloudWatch put-metric errors reducing after 15:40 UTC; STS still intermittent in a subset of AZs. continuing rollout.
bob (sre): latency on Dedicated pools improved ~0.6s -> 0.15s for requests after cache fallback. 5xxs reduced to baseline for routed traffic.
emma (product): posted status update v1 at 15:55 UTC. customer responses minimal so far.
dave (support): two customers acknowledged the note, asking for ETA. advising "monitoring, no ETA until AWS confirms fix".
carla (eng-runtime): AWS reported partial resolution at 16:05 UTC for STS in us-east-1; continuing to observe for stability window. will keep routing preference in place for 30m after stable.
incident-bot: Incident note: mitigations applied (cross-region routing, token-cache fallback), customers notified.
carla (eng-runtime): marking ready for handback to alice if stable for 30m.
alice (oncall): I'm back, confirmed stability over last 35m. reverting routing override in 5m to normal TTLs. preparing post-incident notes.
incident-bot: Incident resolved at 4891008900 (16:35 UTC). Summary: Third-party AWS control-plane (STS/metrics) degradation in us-east-1 caused token refresh and metrics ingest 5xx, impacting Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Mitigations: cross-region routing, token-cache fallback, customer notifications. Postmortem owner: carla.
carla (eng-runtime): starting internal postmortem doc. will include timelines, metrics, and recommendations: automated regional failover, short-circuit token refresh on global control-plane errors, improve customer-impact detection.
emma (product): will coordinate external incident summary for status page and customer comms.
